title: kate-core: indent Python from the text before the caret
summary: python_newline reads only the line text before the caret. A comment line does not gain a unit when it ends in a colon. The existing colon tests stay green. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust in kate-core. Linux CI runs the test. The newline command still calls newline_insertion.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn python_newline(buf: &kate_text::TextBuffer, at: kate_text::Offset, config: &crate::DocumentConfig) -> String

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Read the line from its start through the caret. Ignore the text after the caret. Trim spaces and tabs at the end of that prefix. A colon at the end of the prefix adds one indent unit. A comment line is a line whose first non-indent scalar is #. A comment line keeps its leading indent and does not gain the extra unit. The dead-code attribute stays. newline_insertion stays as it is. The existing python_newline test stays green. Leave keys.rs unchanged. PKT-0079 owns that file. Leave pair.rs unchanged. PKT-0083 owns that file. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: indent::tests::python_newline_reads_only_the_text_before_the_caret
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. In def f(): pass, the caret is Offset(8). The text before the caret ends in a colon, and the result today is only a newline. After the change the result is a newline plus four spaces. In # note:, the caret is at the end, and the result is only a newline. In four spaces, # note:, the caret is at the end, and the result is a newline plus those four spaces.
